assembly_info.comments:
The Basenji dog (Wags) DNA was derived from blood of a single male of central Africa origins (MU ID 185726). His dam, Luka, was an African import and the sire, Logan, has little recent African imports in his pedigree history. Sequences were generated on the Pacific Biosciences Sequel instrument (V2 chemistry) to approximately 45x genome coverage based on a genome size estimate of 2.6 Gb. All SMRT sequences were assembled with the HGAP4 algorithm (SMRT Link v5.0.1.9585) then error corrected using the Arrow error-correction module. Additional polishing of the assembly for residual indels was done by aligning 32x coverage of Illumina data and the Pilon algorithm. Chromosomal level scaffolds were generated with the same DNA source using the ProximoTM Hi-C genome scaffolding software (Phase Genomics Inc) and finalized by alignment to the CanFam3.1 reference. Of the 2.4 Gb assembled genome (Basenji_breed-1.0), the total assembly N50 contig and scaffold lengths are 3.1 Mb and 61.1 Mb, respectively. For questions regarding the use of the Can fam Basenji_breed-1.0 assembly please contact Dr. Wes Warren, Bond Life Sciences Center, University of Missouri, Columbia, MO or Dr. Gary Johnson, University of Missouri, Veterinary School of Medicine, Columbia, MO, USA.
Data use: The Can fam Basenji_breed-1.0 assembly sequence is made available to the community by Dr. Gary Johnson, University of Missouri, Veterinary School of Medicine, Columbia, MO, USA, with the following understanding: Users are free to analyze these data if the providers of this data are properly cited, any whole genome analyses should follow guidelines outlined in the Ft. Lauderdale agreement on the use of this assembly and any redistribution of the data should carry this notice.
